prompt:
Our backup controller needs a small Go integration for the vSAN Data Protection API in VCF 9.0. The package skeleton is already here. Finish Client.CreateSnapshotAndWait so it creates one manual protection-group snapshot and follows the returned task until it reaches a terminal state.

The protected wire contract in docs/contract.json was extracted from specifications/vsan-data-protection/vsan-data-protection-openapi.yaml at the vmware/vcf-api-specs tag 9.0.0.0; docs/official_sources.json pins that tag's commit and the exact operationIds. Implement against those local files. In particular, use the documented /api base path, vmware-api-session-id header, task query, JSON response shapes, and path escaping. CreateSnapshotSpec.Retention is optional: when it is nil, omit the retention member completely rather than sending null or an empty object.

The controller's session token can expire after the snapshot has already been accepted. On a 401, refresh through the supplied TokenSource and replay the failed request with the refreshed token. Keep following the original task identifier; do not create the snapshot again or lose the work already started. Pending, running, and blocked tasks remain in progress, succeeded returns the result, and failed returns an error.

verification_test.go is the acceptance verifier. It runs only against the protected loopback mock in internal/mockdp, which exposes a readable request log and serves only the two operations named by the contract; no VMware appliance or external endpoint is involved. The verifier checks every request's method, URI, authentication header, content type, accept header, and byte-exact body for both absent and present retention. Do not modify verification_test.go, internal/mockdp/server.go, go.mod, or anything under docs/. Run go test -race -timeout 30s ./... until it passes.
